doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: Her music, free jazz and playing
title: Handling distracting thoughts while playing
summary: Through meditation and yoga she lets thoughts come and go and returns to the music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Are you able to not allow irrelevant thoughts to come into your head while you’re playing? That sounded almost like a backward question or something but.

No I understand. I have spent a great deal of time learning how to deal with those thoughts that come up, especially for me in the first ten, fifteen years of playing the thoughts were really just distracting always. Thoughts like oh shouldn’t you play a little bit — shouldn’t you push more or play more or come on — oh what did you play now. You know sort of those critical thoughts that come in. And I have learned over the years to have a different relationship with these thoughts. I realized that thoughts, they’re always going to come up. I can’t shut them off. When you play a concert and you play for two hours, you’re not going to be able to have no, sort of irrelevant or distracting thoughts. And I’ve learned also, through meditation and yoga, to sort of let these thoughts come and go and not hang on to them. It’s the relationship with the thoughts that has changed. Not that I have thoughts or don’t have thoughts. I have thoughts all the time, but

I have learned to not sort of go down the rabbit hole. And I’ve learned to just hear the thought and just refocus, coming back to the music, like in meditation when you focus on the breath and every time a thought comes I sort of let the thought go and I return to the breath. In the music I try to do the same thing. That’s been super helpful for me.
